title: CPU, memory, storage
hook: Your computer keeps data in three places. Close = fast. Far = slow.

steps.caption: You open a photo. The CPU (the part that does the work) looks in RAM first. RAM is fast memory for things you are using right now.

packets.label: Is the photo in fast memory?

nodeCaptions.cpu: CPU does the work. It needs the data close by.
nodeCaptions.ram: RAM is fast memory. It clears when you turn the computer off.

steps.caption: The photo is not in RAM. So the computer looks on the Disk. Disk is where files are saved. It is slower.

nodeCaptions.disk: Disk (or SSD) keeps your files even after you shut down. Slower than RAM.
nodeCaptions.ram: RAM did not have the photo, so it asks the Disk.

steps.caption: Found it. The photo is copied into RAM, then the CPU can show it. Next time it can open faster, because a copy may already be in RAM.

nodeCaptions.ram: A copy stays in RAM for a while. That is why the second open can feel quicker.
nodeCaptions.cpu: Now the CPU has what it needs. Waiting on Disk is what makes apps feel slow.

takeaways: RAM is fast. Disk is slower but keeps your files.
Turn the computer off → RAM clears. Disk still has your files.
Apps feel slow when they keep reading from Disk instead of RAM.

quiz.question: Which is usually faster for the CPU?
quiz.explanation: RAM is close and fast. Disk is farther and slower.

quiz.question: You turn the computer off. What happens?
choices: RAM and Disk both forget everything
RAM clears. Disk still has your files.
quiz.explanation: RAM needs power. Disk keeps files after shutdown.

quiz.question: Why can the same photo open faster the second time?
choices: A copy may already be in RAM
quiz.explanation: After the first open, a copy often sits in RAM.
